title: Sign in (pi.flow)
lede: The embedded pi.flow sign-in: authorize, password, optional MFA, resume, token. Mock PingOne, not a real tenant.

nodes.label: BFF
sub: Holds the PKCE verifier and the session-token cookie. In this lab the page plays this part.

nodes.label: Mock PingOne
sub: Issues flows, codes and mock tokens. Not a real tenant.

nodes.label: Resource server
sub: Mock. Demands acr mock:multi for a transfer.

nodes.label: Mock phone
sub: Stands in for the user's device (CIBA).

steps.title: The form goes to the BFF
steps.what: The user fills in the embedded form. The browser hands the values to the BFF; there is no redirect to a hosted login page.

steps.title: Start the flow
steps.what: GET /authorize with response_mode=pi.flow, PKCE S256, state and nonce. The answer is JSON: a flow in USERNAME_PASSWORD_REQUIRED and an ST cookie.

steps.title: Send the password
steps.what: POST /flows/{id} with the password. The status moves on and the ST cookie is replaced.

steps.title: MFA when demanded
steps.what: Only when MFA is demanded: pick a device, then post the one-time passcode. The cookie rotates again at each step.

steps.title: Resume
steps.what: GET /resume with the current cookie. A stale cookie is refused. The mock answers with an authorization code (UNVERIFIED for a real PingOne).

steps.title: Exchange the code
steps.what: POST /token with the code and the PKCE verifier. The mock answers with id_token and access_token carrying acr, amr, auth_time and nonce.

steps.title: Signed in
steps.what: The BFF tells the browser the user is signed in.
